questions.q: Why is WITH needed to filter a query like 'companies with more than 10 employees' in Cypher?
options: Cypher has no HAVING clause, so WITH is used to compute the aggregate first and then filter on it as an ordinary value in the next stage
WITH is required before every MATCH clause in Cypher, with no exceptions
WHERE cannot be used anywhere in a Cypher query
WITH replaces RETURN entirely in every query
questions.explain: Since Cypher lacks HAVING, WITH lets you compute count(p) first, then treat it like a normal property to filter on afterward.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the `WITH p` line inside a `CALL {}` subquery block?
options: It explicitly imports the outer query's row variable p into the subquery's otherwise isolated scope
It deletes the variable p after the subquery runs
It is optional boilerplate with no functional effect
It converts the subquery into a plain MATCH clause
questions.explain: A CALL {} block is isolated from the outer query by default; WITH p is what explicitly correlates it to the current outer row, similar to a correlated subquery.

questions.q: What is the key difference between MATCH and OPTIONAL MATCH?
options: OPTIONAL MATCH keeps rows even when the pattern doesn't match, filling missing values with null, while plain MATCH drops those rows entirely
OPTIONAL MATCH is faster than MATCH in every case
OPTIONAL MATCH can only be used with numeric properties
There is no real difference between the two clauses
questions.explain: Plain MATCH behaves like an INNER JOIN (drop unmatched rows); OPTIONAL MATCH behaves like a LEFT JOIN (keep the row, null the missing side).

questions.q: In `MATCH (p:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN p.name, c.name`, what happens for a Person with no WORKS_AT relationship?
options: The person is still returned, with c.name coming back as null
The person is excluded from the results entirely
The query throws a runtime error
Cypher automatically creates a WORKS_AT relationship for them
questions.explain: OPTIONAL MATCH preserves the row and returns null for the unmatched part of the pattern, just like an unmatched LEFT JOIN row in T-SQL.

questions.q: What relational-database concept is CALL {} with a WITH import most directly analogous to?
options: A correlated subquery, where the inner query references a value from the current outer row
A CREATE TABLE statement
A non-correlated subquery that ignores the outer query entirely
A database trigger
questions.explain: The lesson draws this exact comparison — WITH p inside CALL {} correlates the subquery to the outer row, the same mechanism a correlated subquery uses in T-SQL.
